messages:
mira: Heads up — since ~09:38 UTC we're seeing intermittent DNS resolve failures from gpu-pool pods in eu-west-1. Node-local-dns metrics show a SERVFAIL spike and ~1-3% UDP packet loss on port 53. This is causing tail latency for inference requests. Anyone else seeing this?

sanjay: same here from canary runner. Started around 09:36. Inference p95 jumps 3x when a resolve hits a retry. Noticed ECMP path spread in traceroute. :thinking:

elaine: grabbed node-local-dns logs and did a quick tcpdump on one affected node. Saw a bunch of truncated UDP responses and repeated retransmits. Also saw some ICMP type 3 (fragmentation needed) which smells like PMTU/MTU mismatch.

devan: interesting — we recently updated flannel MTU on that pool during the GPU scaleup last week. Could be a mismatch between host dev and SR-IOV interfaces. I'll check host iface MTU vs pod MTU.

mira: infra-bot alert posted earlier: "dns-resolves|eu-west-1|node-local-dns - error_rate 2.1% over 5m" 

infra-bot: Alert: dns-resolves high error rate in eu-west-1 (2.1%) — see dashboard https://console.redwood.internal/d/infra/dns?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west-1

sanjay: quick commands I ran:
```
kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/node-local-dns -l k8s-app=node-local-dns --tail=200
tcpdump -i flannel.1 'udp port 53' -w /tmp/dns-flannel.pcap
```

elaine: sample lines from node-local-dns: 
```
E0918 09:37:41.123 svc.go:215] upstream query to 10.0.0.21 failed: write udp 10.0.1.7:53234->10.0.0.21:53: write: message too long
W0918 09:37:41.124 cache.go:98] cache miss for service inference-backend.default.svc.cluster.local
```

devan: "message too long" suggests EDNS / UDP fragmentation. Could be RDMA/MTU interplay on the host. Are we using jumbo frames on the interconnect for that GPU pool?

mira: eu-west GPU pool is on hosts with 9000 MTU to reduce GPU RDMA overhead but some overlay nodes were still at 1500. I flagged a partial rollout last week.

elaine: I forwarded a pcap to sj for analysis. It shows DNS responses with EDNS0 > 1232 bytes, then ICMP frag-needed back. The kernel falls back to retrying and we get retransmits, which the node-local cache treats as timeouts and forwards to upstream -> more retries.

sanjay: mitigation options: 1) force CoreDNS to reply without EDNS (set EDNS0 size to 512), 2) tune node-local-dns to retry fewer times, 3) temporarily disable jumbo frames on hosts to get consistent MTU. Which is least risky?

devan: least risky short-term is patching CoreDNS config to limit EDNS size. Longer term we should make MTU consistent or enable TCP fallback for DNS in node-local-dns. Also consider adding a route to avoid ECMP path with lower MTU.

mira: agree. Can someone submit a quick CoreDNS patch? We can roll it to canaries then the gpu-pool.

elaine: created k8s config change for coredns ConfigMap with `edns0size 512` and tested locally. If we want to force TCP fallback: `upstream_tcp: true` in node-local-dns config — that will increase load but reduce UDP fragmentation issues.

devan: I'm going to run a host-side check across eu-west gpu pool for inconsistent MTU and list nodes with MTU != 9000. Patch queued.

deploy-bot: Started rollout: coredns-configmap patch -> canary (eu-west-1a) at 09:48 UTC. See rollout id r-9523.

mira: noted. Also, this incident is causing autoscaler jitter on gpu-pool because node agents fail healthchecks when DNS fails. That created temporary capacity pressure. Putting a note for SRE: impact = higher tail latency + short autoscaler flaps.

ops-bot: Incident created: INFRA-2023-847 — "Intermittent node-local DNS fragmentation / MTU mismatch causing SERVFAIL and inference tail spikes". Priority P2.

sanjay: after coredns canary (09:50) I see error rate drop from 2.2% -> 0.3% in that AZ. p95 latency for resolve also dropped ~80ms. Looks promising.

elaine: will keep the tcpdump running for 30m and follow up with pcap analysis for root cause. If we confirm inconsistent MTU rollout, we should add a preflight to capacity provisioning that checks host MTU vs overlay MTU.

devan: MTU probe done: 6 hosts out of 120 had 1500 MTU still. Those were added during the last rapid scale and missed the network config script. Filing a follow-on to fix and run a config drift job.

mira: great, thanks team. Next steps: (1) finish coredns rollout if canary stays green, (2) fix MTU drift hosts, (3) add MTU check to scaleup runbook, (4) consider node-local-dns change to prefer TCP fallback for large responses.

elaine: adding logs and pcaps to INFRA-2023-847. Will ping once pcap analysis done. :white_check_mark:
